International Mobility Week The International Mobility Week is an institutional initiative of Guglielmo Marconi University that, within the framework of the University’s internationalization policies, aims to promote awareness of and facilitate access to international mobility opportunities offered by European programs and active academic cooperation agreements. The goal is to provide tools, up-to-date information, and qualified guidance to allow each student to build an international path aligned with their personal and professional ambitions. The week is organized into in-depth sessions, informational meetings, encounters with international partners, and firsthand testimonials, in a format designed to foster awareness, discussion, and planning. The International Mobility Week represents a central element of the University’s internationalization strategy, reflecting a commitment to strengthening participation in Erasmus+ programs, active bilateral agreements, and all forms of mobility recognized today at the European and international level. International Mobility Week December 1 – 5, 2025 From December 1 to 5, 2025, UniMarconi will organize a new edition of the International Mobility Week, entirely dedicated to presenting international mobility programs and exploring study and internship opportunities in the University’s partner countries. The initiative includes an opening plenary session and a series of online thematic meetings, organized by Department and Degree Program, in collaboration with UniMarconi’s international network. Download the event presentations BIP presentation Erasmus presentation The full schedule, including the list of meetings, times, and participation instructions, is available on the dedicated page. degli Studi Guglielmo Marconi participates annually in the Erasmus+ Programme with the objective of fostering the internationalization of its academic offer and strengthening cooperation through agreements and partnerships with Universities across both EU and non-EU countries. For the 2021-2027 programming period, the University successfully renewed its Erasmus Charter for Higher Education (ECHE) , a fundamental prerequisite for participation in mobility initiatives aimed at promoting learning oppportunities and institutional cooperation for innovation within the framework of the Erasmus+ Programme. Participation in the E+ Programme provides UniMarconi students with valuable opportunities to study, undertake traineeships, or gain professional experience abroad. These experiences contribute significantly to the enrichment of students’ academic pathways while enhancing their intercultural competencies and future career prospects in an increasingly globalized labor market. The Programme enables regularly enrolled students to spend a study period at a partner University under existing Bilateral Agreements, either to attend courses or to conduct research related to their final thesis. During their mobility period, students benefit from financial support and receive full academic recognition for the activities successfully completed abroad. Erasmus+ staff – Mobility for academic staff This concerns the mobility of administrative and academic staff to attend training programs abroad, seminars, workshops (staff mobility for training), or to carry out teaching activities at foreign universities (staff mobility for teaching). Erasmus+ Internship – Erasmus Traineeship The Program offers students and graduates the opportunity to complete internships for a maximum period of 12 months at institutions, organizations, companies, or universities located abroad. The Erasmus-supported internship period can also be completed within 12 months after graduation, provided the application is submitted at least one month before the end of studies. degli Studi Guglielmo Marconi participates annually in the Erasmus+ Programme with the objective of fostering the internationalization of its academic offer and strengthening cooperation through agreements and partnerships with Universities across both EU and non-EU countries. For the 2021-2027 programming period, the University successfully renewed its Erasmus Charter for Higher Education (ECHE) , a fundamental prerequisite for participation in mobility initiatives aimed at promoting learning oppportunities and institutional cooperation for innovation within the framework of the Erasmus+ Programme. Participation in the E+ Programme provides UniMarconi students with valuable opportunities to study, undertake traineeships, or gain professional experience abroad. These experiences contribute significantly to the enrichment of students’ academic pathways while enhancing their intercultural competencies and future career prospects in an increasingly globalized labor market. The Programme enables regularly enrolled students to spend a study period at a partner University under existing Bilateral Agreements, either to attend courses or to conduct research related to their final thesis. During their mobility period, students benefit from financial support and receive full academic recognition for the activities successfully completed abroad. Erasmus+ staff – Mobility for academic staff This concerns the mobility of administrative and academic staff to attend training programs abroad, seminars, workshops (staff mobility for training), or to carry out teaching activities at foreign universities (staff mobility for teaching). Erasmus+ Internship – Erasmus Traineeship The Program offers students and graduates the opportunity to complete internships for a maximum period of 12 months at institutions, organizations, companies, or universities located abroad. The Erasmus-supported internship period can also be completed within 12 months after graduation, provided the application is submitted at least one month before the end of studies. Mobility for study – Outgoing Back to Erasmus+ Program The Programme offers students the opportunity to spend a period of time abroad at a Partner University for study purposes or for research related to their degree thesis. To this end, the University signs bilateral agreements with other European universities (Partners) to determine the number of students involved and the fields of study available. Erasmus students receive financial support (a grant) and recognition by their home university of the activities completed (exams) during the period of study abroad. Who can participate All students regularly enrolled in a first- or second-cycle degree program, as well as PhD students. How to participate The University publishes the Erasmus Mobility for Studies call for applications twice a year. The calls can be consulted on the following page: https://www.unimarconi.it/en/erasmus-calls/ Partner Universities: Here you can consult the continuously updated list of Erasmus Partner Universities. Duration of mobility From 2 to 12 months for students of all first- and second-cycle degree programs and for PhD students. From 5 to 30 days (short-term mobility) for PhD students. Eligibility ranking No later than six days after the closing of the Erasmus call for applications, the ranking list is published, including the names of all eligible students and the name of the Partner University that will host them. At the bottom of the ranking list, the deadline for acceptance by the student is indicated. Acceptance of mobility Students included in the ranking list must send the Mobility Acceptance Form , duly completed and signed, to erasmus@unimarconi.it by the deadline indicated at the bottom of the ranking list. Nomination After receiving the Mobility Acceptance Form, the Erasmus Office sends the names of the students awarded the Erasmus+ grant to the relevant host (Partner) universities. Mobility for study – Outgoing Back to Erasmus+ Program The Programme offers students the opportunity to spend a period of time abroad at a Partner University for study purposes or for research related to their degree thesis. To this end, the University signs bilateral agreements with other European universities (Partners) to determine the number of students involved and the fields of study available. Erasmus students receive financial support (a grant) and recognition by their home university of the activities completed (exams) during the period of study abroad. Who can participate All students regularly enrolled in a first- or second-cycle degree program, as well as PhD students. How to participate The University publishes the Erasmus Mobility for Studies call for applications twice a year. The calls can be consulted on the following page: https://www.unimarconi.it/en/erasmus-calls/ Partner Universities: Here you can consult the continuously updated list of Erasmus Partner Universities. Duration of mobility From 2 to 12 months for students of all first- and second-cycle degree programs and for PhD students. From 5 to 30 days (short-term mobility) for PhD students. Eligibility ranking No later than six days after the closing of the Erasmus call for applications, the ranking list is published, including the names of all eligible students and the name of the Partner University that will host them. At the bottom of the ranking list, the deadline for acceptance by the student is indicated. Acceptance of mobility Students included in the ranking list must send the Mobility Acceptance Form , duly completed and signed, to erasmus@unimarconi.it by the deadline indicated at the bottom of the ranking list. Nomination After receiving the Mobility Acceptance Form, the Erasmus Office sends the names of the students awarded the Erasmus+ grant to the relevant host (Partner) universities. As the first fully digital Italian university, Unimarconi builds every day a global community founded on innovation, inclusion, and the promotion of Italian knowledge worldwide. A University open to the world Unimarconi welcomes a community of students and faculty from diverse countries and fosters a growing network of academic partners across Europe, Africa, Asia, and Latin America. Thanks to its digital nature and flexible approach, the University offers an accessible, high-quality education model capable of connecting different cultures, experiences, and perspectives. Its educational offer, multilingual and multidisciplinary, is designed to meet the needs of students from varied backgrounds. Asynchronous courses are available for independent and flexible study, synchronous lessons via live streaming facilitate interaction, blended programs combine digital and in-person learning, and post-graduate in-person pathways are enhanced by the International Student House, a space for intercultural meeting and exchange. A global network of relationships and opportunities Unimarconi’s international strategy develops across five key areas: Africa, where the University promotes institutional partnerships in line with the Mattei Plan and the European Union’s Global Gateway strategy. Europe and the Mediterranean area, through double-degree agreements, co-supervised PhDs, and collaborations with universities and research centers Middle East, particularly Dubai, a rapidly growing educational and cultural hub Southeast Asia, with excellence projects in multiple countries, including Singapore Latin America, with courses and initiatives dedicated to promoting Italian language and culture International recognition In 2025, the Center for World University Rankings (CWUR) included Guglielmo Marconi University among the top 2,000 universities worldwide, out of over 21,000 institutions evaluated. The University ranks within the top 8.3% globally, standing out as the only Italian online university in the ranking. This achievement confirms the strength of the Unimarconi educational model, recognized internationally today, based on teaching quality, graduate employability, scientific productivity, and research impact. A cultural and social mission For Unimarconi, internationalization is not only a growth strategy but also a cultural and social mission. Bringing Italy to the world and opening Italian universities to the world means making education accessible, breaking geographical and economic barriers through technology, and simultaneously highlighting what makes our country unique: culture, language, and a humanistic approach. The goal is to educate not only professionals but global citizens capable of interpreting and leading change, contributing to sustainable community development and the creation of a more equitable and inclusive future. I ROMA21 Università degli Studi Guglielmo Marconi was born and officially accredited by the Ministry of Education University and Research in the year 2004. Its headquarter is located in Rome. Unimarconi counts on 6 faculties, including Bachelor and Master’s Degree programs: School of Business, School of Law, School of Political Sciences, School of Applied Sciences and Technologies, School of Arts, School of Education Science. The offer is enlarged with postgraduate major courses, Phd’s, Double degrees and language courses. The main methodology is the e-learning, thanks to the e-sources and devices provided by the university, ensuring a great flexibility and a high learning quality as well. Università degli studi Guglielmo Marconi Marconi pursues an internationalisation policy aimed at cooperating with foreign Institutions and promoting activities focused on increasing educational, scientific and cultural exchanges and international cooperation. Internationalisation is also aimed at improving the quality and increasing the quantity of mobility, according to the objectives of Europe 2020; in particular, student mobility has a central role. Right to be followed in one’s training path, through orientation, tutoring and counselling activities, according to the predicted ways in the didactic offer. In pursuing knowledge quality improvement, the University aims at achieving and sustaining excellence in every area of teaching and research. One of the objectives of its Strategic Plan is to share a commitment to research excellence, high quality teaching and an outstanding student experience. As a holder of the Erasmus Charter for Higher Education – ECHE with a large network of university partners worldwide, Unimarconi aims at advancing its internationalization strategy through student mobility, research collaboration and cooperation in organizational management. The participation in the Erasmus plus programme will allow our university to achieve some of its internationalisation and modernisation objectives as follows: enhance graduates and researchers skills: participation in activities under the Programme will help Marconi University’s mission to offer students an education of the highest possible quality as well as allowing them to graduate with competencies in demand on the Italian and international labour market. It will also allow the university to be involved in open and innovative interaction with international actors; quality through mobility and cross-border co-operation: Marconi University firmly believes that the major societal challenges are complex and cut across boundaries, sectors and academic specialisations. Therefore, solutions must be found through new interdisciplinary partnerships that cut across boundaries – national as well as academic. The opportunities provided in the Programme will heavily assist in providing mobility and cross-border co-operation. Degree programmes and learning environments must continue to be internationalised, so that cultural diversity and international experiences become strengths to the benefit of all. Programme mobility for both students and staff creates an intercultural learning environment that improves the quality of the university’s degree programmes as well as the students’ learning experiences. knowledge triangle improvement: the combination of high-quality degree programmes and the focus on talent development enhances the university’s competitiveness as well as its ability to contribute to the growth of society. Global collaboration within the Programme will significantly contribute to defining the university’s scope for action and development within this area. The Programme will have a special eye on quality in education and will foster opportunity for benchmarking among partners. This will help the University to reach its objectives and create strong core disciplines and strong degree programmes that make the university an attractive place of study for all students. governance and funding: the benchmarking and development opportunities within the Programme will allow Marconi to strengthen its position as a leading global university. This position will be used to make an impact and to influence international policy development in research, innovation and education both in and outside Europe. From a strong current position, Marconi aims at further improving the quality and level of activity of its research and degrees in coming years. In order to realise this ambition, it is vital to provide the necessary flexibility and freedom for its research activities, which the Programme will contribute to. Need clarification or support? Erasmus Traineeship – Outgoing Back to Erasmus+ Program The Erasmus Traineeship Programme offers students and graduates the opportunity to carry out a traineeship period at institutions, organizations, companies, research centers, universities, etc., located in all countries of the European Union. Non-eligible host organizations are excluded, including: EU institutions and their specialized agencies; organizations managing EU programmes; non-European branches of organizations whose legal headquarters are in one of the countries participating in the programme. The full list is available at: https://europa.eu/about-eu/institutions-bodies/index_it.htm . The Erasmus Traineeship grant varies depending on the destination country. Erasmus Traineeship is an excellent opportunity to gain work placement experience abroad and to enrich one’s CV with new professional, transversal, and language skills. Who can participate Students regularly enrolled: in this case, the traineeship must be fully completed before the discussion of the degree thesis. Final-year students (graduands): provided that they are regularly enrolled and that the application is submitted at least one month before the degree thesis discussion. The traineeship must be carried out within 12 months of obtaining the degree. How to find a host organization To consult the list of Partner Organizations, students may contact the Erasmus Office, which will indicate organizations that have already hosted our students with a high satisfaction rate. Students are also free to independently identify an organization of interest. In any case, it is recommended to gather as much information as possible, including through initial informal contacts, so that the traineeship experience can become a true opportunity for personal and professional growth. There are many websites where internship opportunities can be found, including: ERASMUSINTERN EUROACTIV JOBSITE EURODESK, EU programme information and guidance PRAXIS NETWORK Traineeship agreements How to apply The University publishes Erasmus Traineeship calls for applications twice a year (March and September). These can be consulted on the Erasmus+ Programme page of the University website, where all the steps required to apply are specified. Duration of mobility Mobility for traineeship has a minimum duration of two months and a maximum of 12 months for each cycle of studies. Within these limits, students may decide the duration of the mobility period, also in agreement with the staff of the company or organization where the traineeship will take place. Interview schedule After the closing of the call, the Erasmus Office sets up an interview schedule with students who have applied for traineeship and are deemed eligible according to the call requirements. The interview is both linguistic and motivational and is aimed at identifying suitable host destinations. Required documents: CV and motivation letter. Before departure The Learning Agreement for Traineeship (Mobility Agreement for Traineeship) must be completed only after the formal approval of the traineeship by the Erasmus Office, the host organization, and the student. Grant Completion of the procedure includes payment of the first installment of the grant, equal to 75% of the total amount, by bank transfer before the start of the mobility, as provided for in the financial agreement signed by the student and the University. The total grant amount is calculated based on the duration of the mobility and the monthly amount established for each destination country. Upon return Upon returning from abroad, the student must submit the following documents to the Erasmus Office, which are required for payment of the second installment of the grant: the Learning Agreement for Traineeship , duly completed and signed by the host institution, including in the After the mobility section a description of the skills acquired and results achieved by the student; the Certificate of Attendance , indicating the start and end dates of the mobility, duly signed and stamped by the Erasmus coordinator of the host institution; the Participant Report Form , to be completed in all its parts, which the student receives by email upon return via a dedicated guidance link. Need clarification or support? Back to Erasmus+ Program The new seven-year period 2020-2027 began with a major implementation: EWP – Erasmus Without Paper , a project funded by the European Commission and developed by the European University Foundation, aimed at creating a network for the secure and rapid exchange of data. Universities and all students involved in the Erasmus program will use the main documents relating to Erasmus mobility exclusively in electronic format. Each student will have a single entry point, the Erasmus Mobile App , which will allow them to manage all interactions with their host university and universities, including information on mobility and teaching programs, and, in general, to manage all phases of the mobility: before, during, and after. Students will be periodically updated on the process, which is expected to be completed in the fall. Need clarification or support? Week La International Mobility Week è un’iniziativa istituzionale dell’Università degli Studi Guglielmo Marconi che, nell’ambito delle politiche di internazionalizzazione dell’Ateneo, intende promuovere la conoscenza e facilitare l’accesso alle opportunità di mobilità internazionale offerte dai programmi europei e dagli accordi di cooperazione accademica attivi. L’obiettivo è fornire strumenti, informazioni aggiornate e orientamento qualificato per permettere a ogni studente di costruire un percorso internazionale in linea con le proprie ambizioni personali e professionali. La settimana si articola in momenti di approfondimento, sessioni informative, incontri con partner internazionali e testimonianze dirette, in un format che favorisce consapevolezza, confronto e progettazione. La International Mobility Week rappresenta un tassello centrale della strategia di internazionalizzazione dell’Ateneo, un impegno che punta a rafforzare la partecipazione ai programmi Erasmus+, agli accordi bilaterali attivi e a tutte le forme di mobilità oggi riconosciute a livello europeo e internazionale. International Mobility Week 1 – 5 Dicembre 2025 Dal 1 al 5 dicembre 2025, UniMarconi organizza una nuova edizione della International Mobility Week, interamente dedicata alla presentazione dei programmi di mobilità internazionale e alla scoperta delle opportunità di studio e tirocinio nei Paesi partner dell’Ateneo. L’iniziativa prevede una sessione plenaria di apertura e una serie di incontri tematici online, organizzati per Dipartimento e Corso di Studio, in collaborazione con il network internazionale di UniMarconi. 1 dicembre 2025 – Sessione plenaria Destinatari: studenti e docenti UniMarconi La giornata inaugurale presenta una panoramica completa dei percorsi di mobilità accademica disponibili. Interventi previsti: Saluti istituzionali del Rettore e/o del Delegato del Rettore per le Relazioni Internazionali Presentazione introduttiva dell’Ufficio Relazioni Internazionali Sessione informativa dedicata ai tirocini internazionali Testimonianze di studenti outgoing e incoming Obiettivi: Presentare esperienze dirette di mobilità internazionale Illustrare i programmi Erasmus+ (studio, tirocinio, virtual mobility, virtual exchange, BIP) Chiarire le modalità di riconoscimento delle attività svolte all’estero (OLA, corsi sincroni/asincroni) Fornire informazioni su bandi, requisiti linguistici e application 2, 3 e 4 dicembre 2025 – Sessioni specifiche per Dipartimento e Corso di Studio Destinatari: studenti dei corsi di laurea e laurea magistrale UniMarconi Queste giornate includono incontri tematici online dedicati alle opportunità specifiche per area disciplinare, con la partecipazione dei partner internazionali. Unimarconi scuola Unimarconi cultura Formazione continua Impegno sociale Divulgazione scientifica Eventi di Terza Missione Menu Area Internazionale Home Internazionale Area Internazionale In una realtà accademica che guarda sempre più oltre i confini nazionali, l’Università degli Studi Guglielmo Marconi ha fatto dell’internazionalizzazione uno dei pilastri della propria identità. Primo ateneo digitale italiano, Unimarconi costruisce ogni giorno una comunità globale fondata su innovazione, inclusione e valorizzazione del sapere italiano nel mondo. Un’università aperta al mondo Unimarconi accoglie una comunità di studenti e docenti provenienti da diversi Paesi e coltiva una rete crescente di partner accademici in Europa, Africa, Asia e America Latina. Grazie alla sua natura digitale e al suo approccio flessibile, l’Ateneo offre un modello di istruzione accessibile e di qualità, capace di connettere culture, esperienze e prospettive diverse. L’offerta formativa, multilingue e multidisciplinare, è progettata per rispondere alle esigenze di studenti provenienti da contesti differenti. Sono disponibili corsi asincroni per uno studio autonomo e flessibile, lezioni sincrone in live streaming per favorire l’interazione, programmi blended che combinano digitale e presenza, e percorsi post-lauream in presenza, arricchiti dalla International Student House , luogo di incontro e scambio interculturale. Una rete globale di relazioni e opportunità La strategia internazionale di Unimarconi si sviluppa su cinque aree chiave: Africa, dove l’Ateneo promuove partnership istituzionali in linea con il Piano Mattei e la strategia Global Gateway dell’Unione Europea Europa e area mediterranea, con accordi di doppio titolo, co-tutele per dottorati e collaborazioni con università e centri di ricerca Medio Oriente, in particolare Dubai, hub formativo e culturale in rapida crescita Sud-Est Asiatico, con progetti di eccellenza in numerosi paesi tra cui Singapore America Latina, con iniziative dedicate alla diffusione della lingua e cultura italiana Riconoscimento internazionale Nel 2025, il Center for World University Rankings (CWUR) ha inserito l’Università degli Studi Guglielmo Marconi tra le prime 2.000 università al mondo, su oltre 21.000 istituzioni valutate. L’Ateneo si colloca nel top 8,3% a livello globale, distinguendosi come unica università telematica italiana presente in classifica. Guglielmo Marconi partecipa ogni anno al Programma Erasmus con l’obiettivo di promuovere l’internazionalizzazione dell’offerta formativa e di sviluppare accordi e collaborazioni con le altre Università UE ed extra UE. L’Università per il periodo 2021-2027 ha ottenuto il rinnovo della Erasmus Charter for Higher Education (ECHE) , documento necessario per la partecipazione ad iniziative di mobilità per l’apprendimento e di cooperazione per l’innovazione nell’ambito del Programma Erasmus+. Partecipando ad uno dei Programmi Erasmus gli studenti Unimarconi hanno l’opportunità di studiare, formarsi oppure lavorare all’estero con la possibilità di arricchire il proprio curriculum e di ampliare le prospettive per la propria carriera. Il Programma offre agli studenti regolarmente iscritti la possibilità di trascorrere all’estero un periodo di tempo presso una Università Partner (Accordi bilaterali Erasmus) per motivi di studio o per ricerca sulla tesi di laurea. Lo studente riceve un contributo finanziario e il riconoscimento delle attività completate durante il periodo Erasmus. Erasmus+ staff – Mobility for academic staff Riguarda la mobilità del personale amministrativo ed accademico per seguire percorsi di formazione all’estero, seminari, workshop (staff mobility for training) o per svolgere attività di insegnamento negli atenei esteri (staff mobility for teaching) . Erasmus+ Tirocinio – Erasmus Traineeship Il Programma offre agli studenti e ai laureati la possibilità di svolgere per un periodo massimo di 12 mesi attività di stage/tirocinio presso Istituzioni, Enti, Aziende, Università aventi sede all’estero. Il periodo di tirocinio all’estero con il contributo Erasmus può essere realizzato anche nei 12 mesi successivi al conseguimento della laurea purché la domanda venga trasmessa entro un mese prima dalla conclusione degli studi. Guglielmo Marconi partecipa ogni anno al Programma Erasmus con l’obiettivo di promuovere l’internazionalizzazione dell’offerta formativa e di sviluppare accordi e collaborazioni con le altre Università UE ed extra UE. L’Università per il periodo 2021-2027 ha ottenuto il rinnovo della Erasmus Charter for Higher Education (ECHE) , documento necessario per la partecipazione ad iniziative di mobilità per l’apprendimento e di cooperazione per l’innovazione nell’ambito del Programma Erasmus+. Partecipando ad uno dei Programmi Erasmus gli studenti Unimarconi hanno l’opportunità di studiare, formarsi oppure lavorare all’estero con la possibilità di arricchire il proprio curriculum e di ampliare le prospettive per la propria carriera. Il Programma offre agli studenti regolarmente iscritti la possibilità di trascorrere all’estero un periodo di tempo presso una Università Partner (Accordi bilaterali Erasmus) per motivi di studio o per ricerca sulla tesi di laurea. Lo studente riceve un contributo finanziario e il riconoscimento delle attività completate durante il periodo Erasmus. Erasmus+ staff – Mobility for academic staff Riguarda la mobilità del personale amministrativo ed accademico per seguire percorsi di formazione all’estero, seminari, workshop (staff mobility for training) o per svolgere attività di insegnamento negli atenei esteri (staff mobility for teaching) . Erasmus+ Tirocinio – Erasmus Traineeship Il Programma offre agli studenti e ai laureati la possibilità di svolgere per un periodo massimo di 12 mesi attività di stage/tirocinio presso Istituzioni, Enti, Aziende, Università aventi sede all’estero. Il periodo di tirocinio all’estero con il contributo Erasmus può essere realizzato anche nei 12 mesi successivi al conseguimento della laurea purché la domanda venga trasmessa entro un mese prima dalla conclusione degli studi. Erasmus+ L’Università degli Studi Guglielmo Marconi partecipa ogni anno al Programma Erasmus con l’obiettivo di promuovere l’internazionalizzazione dell’offerta formativa e di sviluppare accordi e collaborazioni con le altre Università UE ed extra UE. L’Università per il periodo 2021-2027 ha ottenuto il rinnovo della Erasmus Charter for Higher Education (ECHE) , documento necessario per la partecipazione ad iniziative di mobilità per l’apprendimento e di cooperazione per l’innovazione nell’ambito del Programma Erasmus+. Partecipando ad uno dei Programmi Erasmus gli studenti Unimarconi hanno l’opportunità di studiare, formarsi oppure lavorare all’estero con la possibilità di arricchire il proprio curriculum e di ampliare le prospettive per la propria carriera. Il Programma offre agli studenti regolarmente iscritti la possibilità di trascorrere all’estero un periodo di tempo presso una Università Partner (Accordi bilaterali Erasmus) per motivi di studio o per ricerca sulla tesi di laurea. Lo studente riceve un contributo finanziario e il riconoscimento delle attività completate durante il periodo Erasmus. Erasmus+ staff – Mobility for academic staff Riguarda la mobilità del personale amministrativo ed accademico per seguire percorsi di formazione all’estero, seminari, workshop (staff mobility for training) o per svolgere attività di insegnamento negli atenei esteri (staff mobility for teaching) . Erasmus+ Tirocinio – Erasmus Traineeship Il Programma offre agli studenti e ai laureati la possibilità di svolgere per un periodo massimo di 12 mesi attività di stage/tirocinio presso Istituzioni, Enti, Aziende, Università aventi sede all’estero. Il periodo di tirocinio all’estero con il contributo Erasmus può essere realizzato anche nei 12 mesi successivi al conseguimento della laurea purché la domanda venga trasmessa entro un mese prima dalla conclusione degli studi. Apply Alias Careers Guglielmo Marconi University introduces the Alias Careers program, aimed at ensuring respect, dignity, and privacy for students who need to adopt a “chosen” name different from their official legal name during their academic experience. The Alias Careers program allows for the creation of a parallel identity, recognized exclusively within the University, to facilitate an inclusive pathway for students undergoing gender transition, enabling them to experience university life in harmony with their chosen identity. How to Activate an Alias Career To initiate the activation process for an Alias Career, interested students must send a request by email to carriera.alias@unimarconi.it , attaching: The application form for activating the Alias Career ; A copy of a valid identity document; A recent passport-style photograph. The Student Office will forward all information and required documentation to the Rector or their delegate for approval. Once the application is accepted, an “Alias Career Confidentiality Agreement” will be signed between the student and the University. Subsequently, the Student Office will proceed with activating the Alias Career in accordance with the guidelines established by the University Regulations. Apply Alias Careers Guglielmo Marconi University introduces the Alias Careers program, aimed at ensuring respect, dignity, and privacy for students who need to adopt a “chosen” name different from their official legal name during their academic experience. The Alias Careers program allows for the creation of a parallel identity, recognized exclusively within the University, to facilitate an inclusive pathway for students undergoing gender transition, enabling them to experience university life in harmony with their chosen identity. How to Activate an Alias Career To initiate the activation process for an Alias Career, interested students must send a request by email to carriera.alias@unimarconi.it , attaching: The application form for activating the Alias Career ; A copy of a valid identity document; A recent passport-style photograph. The Student Office will forward all information and required documentation to the Rector or their delegate for approval. Once the application is accepted, an “Alias Career Confidentiality Agreement” will be signed between the student and the University. Subsequently, the Student Office will proceed with activating the Alias Career in accordance with the guidelines established by the University Regulations. Organized by UniMarconi in collaboration with leading companies, the program offers bimonthly events focused on market trends, training in specific skills, and professional networking. Experts and Partner Companies Each event will host prominent managers and professionals from leading companies, who will share experiences and practical advice to help participants better navigate their professional paths. Project Objectives Career Orientation and Labor Market Analysis Provide a clear overview of major trends and future challenges. Development of Key Skills Provide essential technical and transversal tools for professional success. Building Contact Networks romote networking with professionals and companies. We Will Talk About Labor market: trends and innovations New professions and job search strategies Networking and personal branding Upskilling and reskilling: challenges of the market Soft skills and leadership Innovation, sustainability, and digital transformation Diversity, equity, and inclusion Recruitment and selection Calendar Details Meetings will be held every two months, from 5:00 p.m. to 6:00 p.m. , both in person and via streaming. Each session will focus on a specific topic and provide practical insights thanks to the participation of industry experts. Organized by UniMarconi in collaboration with leading companies, the program offers bimonthly events focused on market trends, training in specific skills, and professional networking. Experts and Partner Companies Each event will host prominent managers and professionals from leading companies, who will share experiences and practical advice to help participants better navigate their professional paths. Project Objectives Career Orientation and Labor Market Analysis Provide a clear overview of major trends and future challenges. Development of Key Skills Provide essential technical and transversal tools for professional success. Building Contact Networks romote networking with professionals and companies. We Will Talk About Labor market: trends and innovations New professions and job search strategies Networking and personal branding Upskilling and reskilling: challenges of the market Soft skills and leadership Innovation, sustainability, and digital transformation Diversity, equity, and inclusion Recruitment and selection Calendar Details Meetings will be held every two months, from 5:00 p.m. to 6:00 p.m. , both in person and via streaming. Each session will focus on a specific topic and provide practical insights thanks to the participation of industry experts. How to Participate Participation is free and open to all interested students and recent graduates. Registration is required via the form published on the page of each individual event. Resources for Participants At the end of each meeting, participants will receive in-depth materials and useful resources . Academy Paolo Graldi in collaboration with Il Messaggero Academy Paolo Graldi in collaboration with Il Messaggero The Paolo Graldi Academy in collaboration with Il Messaggero was created to offer innovative and highly specialized training programs in journalism, communication, and digital media. This partnership combines the academic rigor of Università Guglielmo Marconi , Italy’s first fully digital university, with the real-world experience of Il Messaggero , a historic newspaper that for over 147 years has been one of the most authoritative voices in Italian journalism. Excellence in Media and Communication Training The Academy offers a university Master’s program and specialized training courses designed to provide an integrated view of traditional information and new digital frontiers. The programs are structured to respond to profound changes in the sector, emphasizing professional ethics, high-quality content, and technological innovation. At the heart of the project is the ambition to train professionals who are knowledgeable, skilled, and capable of addressing the challenges of contemporary information with competence. About Il Messaggero Il Messaggero is the leading newspaper of Caltagirone Editore , which also publishes Il Mattino , Il Gazzettino , Corriere Adriatico , Quotidiano di Puglia , and Leggo , Italy’s first social press. Six national newspapers with over thirty local editorial offices in Lazio, Umbria, Abruzzo, Campania, Veneto, Marche, and Puglia work to provide hundreds of thousands of readers with timely, objective, and verified information. Since 2020, this offering has been enriched with four monthly magazines— MoltoSalute , MoltoDonna , MoltoFuturo , and MoltoEconomia —produced with contributions from the most qualified journalists of the six Group newspapers. Digital information is equally competitive, with IlMessaggero.it consistently ranking third among Italian news websites by users, and the other Group sites holding leading positions in their respective geographic areas. innovative and highly specialized training programs in journalism, communication, and digital media. This partnership combines the academic rigor of Università Guglielmo Marconi , Italy’s first fully digital university, with the real-world experience of Il Messaggero , a historic newspaper that for over 147 years has been one of the most authoritative voices in Italian journalism. Excellence in Media and Communication Training The Academy offers a university Master’s program and specialized training courses designed to provide an integrated view of traditional information and new digital frontiers. The programs are structured to respond to profound changes in the sector, emphasizing professional ethics, high-quality content, and technological innovation. At the heart of the project is the ambition to train professionals who are knowledgeable, skilled, and capable of addressing the challenges of contemporary information with competence. About Il Messaggero Il Messaggero is the leading newspaper of Caltagirone Editore , which also publishes Il Mattino , Il Gazzettino , Corriere Adriatico , Quotidiano di Puglia , and Leggo , Italy’s first social press. Six national newspapers with over thirty local editorial offices in Lazio, Umbria, Abruzzo, Campania, Veneto, Marche, and Puglia work to provide hundreds of thousands of readers with timely, objective, and verified information. Since 2020, this offering has been enriched with four monthly magazines— MoltoSalute , MoltoDonna , MoltoFuturo , and MoltoEconomia —produced with contributions from the most qualified journalists of the six Group newspapers. Digital information is equally competitive, with IlMessaggero.it consistently ranking third among Italian news websites by users, and the other Group sites holding leading positions in their respective geographic areas. (DSEAGP) The Department of Economic and Business, Legal and Political Sciences (DSEAGP) was established by Rectoral Decree no. 1 of 27 February 2025, following the merger of the Department of Economic and Business Sciences and the Department of Legal and Political Sciences, inheriting their scientific, educational, and project-related experience. The Department is conceived as a dynamic and interdisciplinary entity, bringing together economic, business, legal, political, and historical expertise, with the aim of interpreting and supporting the transformations of contemporary society from both a national and international perspective. Read more The economic-business area promotes and coordinates scientific research on economic and business topics, with particular attention to current trends and the impact of new technologies. Research lines cover, among other subjects, international management and marketing, with a focus on country branding and Made in Italy, consumer behavior, and business strategies increasingly oriented toward sustainability and technological innovation, including artificial intelligence. Another area of interest is the organization and management of human resources, analyzed in light of digital transformation processes and principles of social inclusion and circular economy. Equally important is the study of economic development, approached through theoretical models related to global cooperation and climate change. Analysis also extends to the banking and financial system, with a focus on banking regulation, international monetary policies, and financing instruments for small and medium-sized enterprises. Research activities are conducted at various levels, from micro to macro, considering subjects such as consumers, companies, corporate groups, real and financial markets, and national and supranational economic systems. Regarding education, the economic-business area addresses the growing demand for professional profiles in managerial and economic-financial sectors, offering a comprehensive and specialized educational pathway. The goal is to facilitate graduates’ entry into diverse contexts, ranging from private companies to public administrations, financial institutions, territorial organizations, trade unions and professional bodies, and national and international research centers. The Department also encourages the continuation of studies in subsequent cycles, thanks to a rich offering of post-graduate courses. The legal-political area of the Department promotes and coordinates research activities in the legal and political fields, combining theoretical depth with the analysis of practical implications of the institutions studied. Research covers legal institutions from substantive, procedural, and judicial perspectives, considering their interaction with European and international contexts, as well as public and corporate dimensions. Significant attention is also given to the analysis of political and social phenomena, studied in their historical evolution and their most recent theoretical and empirical aspects, with particular focus on crime, political communication, electoral trends, and the history of political thought. Complementing this are studies on the political and social history of the contemporary era, with particular reference to the history of institutions, diplomatic relations, and globalization processes. In the legal-political field as well, the educational offer aims to prepare professionals with solid skills, destined to work in the legal profession, public administration, companies, territorial organizations, research institutions, and international organizations. The Department supports and promotes further studies in second- and third-level pathways through a comprehensive offering of post-graduate courses. The entire teaching staff of the Department shares a vision oriented toward developing interdisciplinary research capable of investigating, in an integrated way, the transformations of the legal, economic, political, and institutional systems, following a comparative and international approach. Within this perspective is also the PhD in Legal and Political Sciences , coordinated by Professor Ulrike Haider Quercia, distinguished by its multidisciplinary approach and alignment with the Department’s research lines. The Department has two editorial series: one produced in collaboration with the publisher ES of Naples, and the other with the University’s own publishing house. Among the initiatives promoted, the Dante Cosi Award , established in memory of the Dean of the Faculty of Education Sciences who passed away prematurely, stands out. The award is given annually to deserving students and PhD candidates, who deliver a public lecture during the award ceremony. The Department also hosts the Research and Third Mission Committee (RTM) , which assists the Director in defining and monitoring strategic objectives in scientific research and third mission activities. The Committee is responsible for reviewing activities, identifying strengths and weaknesses, and proposing improvements. Its members are Professors M. Bagarani (Chair), G. Carallo, D. Ceccarelli Morolli, M.A. Icolari, and M. Panci. The Departmental Fund Allocation Committee consists of members of the Departmental Board, currently composed of the Director, Professor Andrea Ungari, the Vice Director, Professor Michela Matarazzo, and Professors Nunzio Casalino, Francesco Gaspari, Renato Giovannini, and Marzia Rossi. Departmental contacts are: Professor Marzia Rossi for teaching, Professor Bruno Marsigalia for research, Professor Enrico Maria Cervellati for internationalization, Professor Riccardo Restuccia for third mission and social impact, Professor Maria Assunta Icolari for quality assurance processes, and Professor Cristina Santini for projects. Completing the team are representatives of PhD candidates, research fellows, and post-docs — Dr. Luca Sbranti, Dr. Greta Spreafico, and Dr. Leila Tavi — and student representatives: Dr. Francesco Elia De Petris, Dr. Mikel Menozzi Dos Santos, Dr. Federico Di Bartolo, Dr. Luca Pichierri, Dr. Serena Quercioli, Dr. Davide Ricciardi, and Dr. Sonia Targhetta. Organization Professors Documents and regulations Research Areas and lines of research Research projects Research outputs and results Teaching Since its establishment, the Department of Economic and Business, Legal and Political Sciences of UniMarconi has based its teaching approach on three fundamental pillars: flexibility, innovation, and inclusion . Flexibility , because our ten degree programs and over twenty curricula allow each student to build a tailor-made educational path, in line with their learning objectives and professional growth goals. Innovation , because we have always valued the potential of new technologies, from the web to artificial intelligence, to enhance the study experience and support the achievement of learning outcomes. Inclusion , because quality teaching is teaching that, while striving for excellence, guarantees everyone the same opportunities for learning and success. (DSEAGP) The Department of Economic and Business, Legal and Political Sciences (DSEAGP) was established by Rectoral Decree no. 1 of 27 February 2025, following the merger of the Department of Economic and Business Sciences and the Department of Legal and Political Sciences, inheriting their scientific, educational, and project-related experience. The Department is conceived as a dynamic and interdisciplinary entity, bringing together economic, business, legal, political, and historical expertise, with the aim of interpreting and supporting the transformations of contemporary society from both a national and international perspective. Read more The economic-business area promotes and coordinates scientific research on economic and business topics, with particular attention to current trends and the impact of new technologies. Research lines cover, among other subjects, international management and marketing, with a focus on country branding and Made in Italy, consumer behavior, and business strategies increasingly oriented toward sustainability and technological innovation, including artificial intelligence. Another area of interest is the organization and management of human resources, analyzed in light of digital transformation processes and principles of social inclusion and circular economy. Equally important is the study of economic development, approached through theoretical models related to global cooperation and climate change. Analysis also extends to the banking and financial system, with a focus on banking regulation, international monetary policies, and financing instruments for small and medium-sized enterprises. Research activities are conducted at various levels, from micro to macro, considering subjects such as consumers, companies, corporate groups, real and financial markets, and national and supranational economic systems. Regarding education, the economic-business area addresses the growing demand for professional profiles in managerial and economic-financial sectors, offering a comprehensive and specialized educational pathway. The goal is to facilitate graduates’ entry into diverse contexts, ranging from private companies to public administrations, financial institutions, territorial organizations, trade unions and professional bodies, and national and international research centers. The Department also encourages the continuation of studies in subsequent cycles, thanks to a rich offering of post-graduate courses. The legal-political area of the Department promotes and coordinates research activities in the legal and political fields, combining theoretical depth with the analysis of practical implications of the institutions studied. Research covers legal institutions from substantive, procedural, and judicial perspectives, considering their interaction with European and international contexts, as well as public and corporate dimensions. Significant attention is also given to the analysis of political and social phenomena, studied in their historical evolution and their most recent theoretical and empirical aspects, with particular focus on crime, political communication, electoral trends, and the history of political thought. Complementing this are studies on the political and social history of the contemporary era, with particular reference to the history of institutions, diplomatic relations, and globalization processes. In the legal-political field as well, the educational offer aims to prepare professionals with solid skills, destined to work in the legal profession, public administration, companies, territorial organizations, research institutions, and international organizations. The Department supports and promotes further studies in second- and third-level pathways through a comprehensive offering of post-graduate courses. The entire teaching staff of the Department shares a vision oriented toward developing interdisciplinary research capable of investigating, in an integrated way, the transformations of the legal, economic, political, and institutional systems, following a comparative and international approach. Within this perspective is also the PhD in Legal and Political Sciences , coordinated by Professor Ulrike Haider Quercia, distinguished by its multidisciplinary approach and alignment with the Department’s research lines. The Department has two editorial series: one produced in collaboration with the publisher ES of Naples, and the other with the University’s own publishing house. Among the initiatives promoted, the Dante Cosi Award , established in memory of the Dean of the Faculty of Education Sciences who passed away prematurely, stands out. The award is given annually to deserving students and PhD candidates, who deliver a public lecture during the award ceremony. The Department also hosts the Research and Third Mission Committee (RTM) , which assists the Director in defining and monitoring strategic objectives in scientific research and third mission activities. The Committee is responsible for reviewing activities, identifying strengths and weaknesses, and proposing improvements. Its members are Professors M. Bagarani (Chair), G. Carallo, D. Ceccarelli Morolli, M.A. Icolari, and M. Panci. The Departmental Fund Allocation Committee consists of members of the Departmental Board, currently composed of the Director, Professor Andrea Ungari, the Vice Director, Professor Michela Matarazzo, and Professors Nunzio Casalino, Francesco Gaspari, Renato Giovannini, and Marzia Rossi. Departmental contacts are: Professor Marzia Rossi for teaching, Professor Bruno Marsigalia for research, Professor Enrico Maria Cervellati for internationalization, Professor Riccardo Restuccia for third mission and social impact, Professor Maria Assunta Icolari for quality assurance processes, and Professor Cristina Santini for projects. Completing the team are representatives of PhD candidates, research fellows, and post-docs — Dr. Luca Sbranti, Dr. Greta Spreafico, and Dr. Leila Tavi — and student representatives: Dr. Francesco Elia De Petris, Dr. Mikel Menozzi Dos Santos, Dr. Federico Di Bartolo, Dr. Luca Pichierri, Dr. Serena Quercioli, Dr. Davide Ricciardi, and Dr. Sonia Targhetta. Organization Professors Documents and regulations Research Areas and lines of research Research projects Research outputs and results Teaching Since its establishment, the Department of Economic and Business, Legal and Political Sciences of UniMarconi has based its teaching approach on three fundamental pillars: flexibility, innovation, and inclusion . Flexibility , because our ten degree programs and over twenty curricula allow each student to build a tailor-made educational path, in line with their learning objectives and professional growth goals. Innovation , because we have always valued the potential of new technologies, from the web to artificial intelligence, to enhance the study experience and support the achievement of learning outcomes. Inclusion , because quality teaching is teaching that, while striving for excellence, guarantees everyone the same opportunities for learning and success.
